metadata.file_name: 117. Lim et al. (2024). Exploration of Variables Predicting Sense of School Belonging Using the Machine Learning Method—Group Mnet.pdf
metadata.title: Exploration of Variables Predicting Sense of School Belonging Using the Machine Learning Method—Group Mnet

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2015 microdata for Korean students and constructs a modeling dataset by merging four questionnaires (student background, ICT familiarity, educational career, and parent). The authors explicitly removed weighting variables (e.g., W_FSTURWT) during preprocessing, along with identification and administration variables, and then restricted the plausible values by retaining only the first PV per subject while deleting the other PVs. They further removed variables with ≥30% missingness and near-zero variance variables, and then applied k-nearest neighbors (k-NN) imputation to handle remaining missingness. Because the manuscript does not report applying PISA complex survey weights (and the weighting variable was removed), the ML models are treated as unweighted analyses; this may affect generalizability and uncertainty estimates under the clustered sampling design.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Analytic sample is Korean students participating in PISA 2015 (n=5581; most are 10th graders). The authors began with 927 student and parent variables after merging four questionnaires, removed irrelevant variables including identification (e.g., CNTSTUID), weighting (e.g., W_FSTURWT), and administration (e.g., ADMINMODE), and retained only the first plausible value (PV1) for each subject while deleting other PVs. They then deleted variables with ≥30% missingness (68 variables), removed near-zero variance variables (65 variables), removed derived variables (56 variables such as ANXTEST and MOTIVA) and instead included individual items, yielding 504 variables. For missingness in the remaining predictors, they used k-NN imputation after listwise deletion would have retained only ~8.13% of observations (454/5581).

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2015 (KOR; most students in grade 10) — school belonging (ST034)
top_predictors: Teacher insulted in front of others
main_findings.performance_metrics: Group Mnet — test RMSE stable across 100 iterations: range 0.36–0.41, mean 0.39 (SD=0.009). Average selected variables per run: 74.55 (SD=22.14) out of 504; ~14.8% selected per run.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2015 (KOR) the study leveraged student gender, home ICT resources, perceived school climate threats, teacher treatment, and life satisfaction to predict students’ sense of school belonging (ST034), finding that predictors spanning background, school climate, peer/teacher relationships, parental involvement, motivation/anxiety, ICT attitudes, and learning/physical activities contributed to prediction with stable test RMSE (≈0.39). This indicates that strengthening supportive school climate and positive teacher–peer relationships, alongside targeted supports for students’ motivation and anxiety, may improve school belonging, though the results are predictive and do not establish causal effects.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes PISA 2015 Korean student data to predict students’ sense of school belonging measured by ST034 (4-point Likert; Cronbach’s alpha = .80). After preprocessing (removing identification/administration/weighting variables, retaining only the first PV per subject, deleting variables with ≥30% missingness and near-zero variance, and using k-NN imputation for remaining missingness), the authors fit Group Mnet, a penalized regression method designed for grouped dummy-coded predictors and multicollinearity. Model performance was assessed via repeated random train/test splits (70/30) with 10-fold CV on training to select the penalty, repeated 100 times; test RMSE was stable at a mean of 0.39 (SD=0.009). Across runs, Mnet selected on average 74.55 variables (≈14.8% of 504), and 32 variables were selected in ≥75 iterations, spanning student, parent, peer/teacher, ICT, and learning/physical activity domains. Limitations include unweighted ML estimation (PISA weights removed/not applied) and the fact that penalized selection counts identify predictive contribution rather than statistical significance or causality.
